6. Event, organizer, and news information

What the listings are. Inner Network aggregates information about professional events from organizers' public websites and event pages, and headlines from industry news publishers. We publish factual details (what, when, where, who is organizing it, price, and a link to register), a short excerpt (about 300 characters) of the organizer's description with a link to the organizer's page for the full text, and the names of speakers the organizer has announced. News items are shown as a headline, a short excerpt, the publisher's name, and a link to the publisher's article.

We are not the organizer. We do not organize, host, sponsor, promote, sell tickets for, or guarantee any event we list, and we are not affiliated with, endorsed by, or authorized by any organizer, venue, or publisher unless we say so expressly. Event details change, events are cancelled, and organizers' pages are sometimes wrong or out of date. Always confirm details with the organizer before you make plans, buy tickets, or travel. Registration, tickets, refunds, admission, and everything that happens at an event are solely between you and the organizer.

Organizer listings and the "Claimed" badge. Organizer profiles are created from public information or by members. An organizer can ask to claim its listing. The "Claimed by this organization" badge means that we approved a claim request after a person told us they represent the organization and provided a contact email; it does not mean we have independently verified that person's authority.

Names, logos, and trademarks. Organizer, venue, publisher, and company names and logos that appear in the Service are trademarks of their respective owners. We use them only to identify the organization and link to its official site. Their appearance does not mean that the organization sponsors or endorses Inner Network, or that we are affiliated with it. We do not alter logos other than resizing them. If you own a name or logo shown in the Service and want it changed or removed, or want to claim your listing, tell us using the Report option or our Content Removal and Correction Policy and we will act promptly.

Our content. Our own compilation of listings, the way they are organized, and our software and designs belong to us. Organizer descriptions (including the excerpts we show), logos, and news excerpts belong to their owners and are displayed to identify and describe the event or article.

15. Dispute resolution: binding individual arbitration and class action waiver

Please read this section carefully. It requires you to arbitrate disputes with us on an individual basis and limits the ways you can seek relief. This section is marked for review by a licensed Florida attorney before it is relied upon.

Informal resolution first. Before starting arbitration or any other proceeding, you agree to email us at contact@innernetwork.app with a description of the dispute and what you want, and we agree to do the same to you. We will each try in good faith to resolve the dispute within 60 days of that notice. If we cannot, either of us may start arbitration as described below.

Agreement to arbitrate. Except for the exceptions below, you and Wavecode agree that any dispute, claim, or controversy arising out of or relating to these Terms, the Privacy Policy, or the Service, including claims about their formation, validity, or scope, will be resolved by binding arbitration before a single neutral arbitrator, and not in court. The Federal Arbitration Act governs this agreement. The arbitration will be administered by the American Arbitration Association ("AAA") under its Consumer Arbitration Rules then in effect (available at adr.org), as modified by this section. The arbitrator may award the same individual relief a court could, must follow these Terms, and will issue a reasoned written decision. Judgment on the award may be entered in any court with jurisdiction. Arbitration fees will be allocated under the AAA rules; where the rules require us to pay more of the fees than you, we will. The arbitration will take place in Miami-Dade County, Florida, or by video or telephone if you prefer, or in a location the AAA rules provide for individual consumers.

Exceptions. Either of us may (a) bring an individual claim in small claims court if it qualifies, and (b) seek an injunction or other equitable relief in court to protect intellectual property rights or to stop unauthorized use of the Service, without first arbitrating.

Class action waiver. You and Wavecode agree that each may bring claims against the other only in an individual capacity and not as a plaintiff or class member in any purported class, collective, consolidated, or representative proceeding. The arbitrator may not consolidate more than one person's claims or preside over any form of class or representative proceeding. If this class action waiver is found unenforceable as to a particular claim, then that claim (and only that claim) must be brought in court rather than in arbitration, and the remaining claims will still be arbitrated.

Jury trial waiver. To the extent any dispute proceeds in court rather than arbitration, you and Wavecode each waive any right to a jury trial, to the extent permitted by law.

Your right to opt out. You can reject this arbitration agreement and class action waiver by emailing contact@innernetwork.app with the subject "Arbitration opt-out" within 30 days after you first accept these Terms, stating your full name, the email on your account, and that you want to opt out of arbitration. Opting out does not affect any other part of these Terms and does not affect any earlier arbitration agreement you may have agreed to.

Changes. If we change this Section 15 after you accepted these Terms, you may reject the change by emailing us within 30 days of the change taking effect, in which case the version of this section you previously accepted will continue to apply to disputes with us.
